newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares end nearly flat, A shares fall.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares end nearly flat, A shares fall.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index ended little changed on Thursday with bargain-hunting continuing to support the market but the A share index closed sharply down on weak investor confidence, traders said.
The B index edged up 0.091 points or 0.14 percent to 64.343 points on volume of 55.5 million shares worth $20.4 million.

But the A share index fell 75.693 points or 7.54 percent to 940.548 points on volume of 788.7 million shares worth 2.0 billion yuan. Brokers said retail investors on the A market used opportunity of a technical rebound on Wednesday to offset their positions, indicating sentiment was still weak.
Shanghai A shares plunged on unstable market sentiment and some panic selling was seen on rumors that more negative market news will be announced at the weekend, brokers said.
The SSE 30 index slumped 99.042 points or 3.97 percent to 2393.810 points.
Of 42 B shares, 41 traded with 16 up, three flat and 22 down.

Brokers said that the A share falls had little impact on their B counterparts. There was some B share profit-taking selling after yesterday's rise, but the basically strong market sentiment remained intact with active bargain-hunting.
"Falls in the A shares has limited impact on long-term investors of cheaper B shares," one broker said.
"Technical charts show the B share index is likely to consolidate between 63 and 65 points in the short term with investors targeting stocks with strong profits records," a second broker said.
Inner Mongolia Erdos Cashmere was the star on expectation of good results, rising $0.052 or 9.84 percent to $0.580, on volume of 1.7 million shares.
Shanghai Tyre & Rubber followed on institutional buying, up $0.034 or 8.21 percent to $0.448, on volume of 1.2 million shares.
China Textile Machinery traded the most on institutional liquidation selling on expected poor results, falling $0.016 or 8.98 percent to $0.162, on volume of 3.2 million shares.
